recipe.positive: Edo-period-inspired multi-block woodblock colour print technique: confident, even-weight black key lines carved with a knife and printed as solid opaque ink, with a few tiny angular nicks, slightly rough ink edges, and faint wood-grain streaks inside larger black areas; flat colour fields built from separate blocks on handmade washi paper; soft bokashi gradation only at sky, water or cloth-hem edges; visible warm cream washi ground with long wispy plant fibres and faint ink-absorption mottling; flattened perspective and shallow stage-like space with bold asymmetrical composition and cropped bands; patterned textiles, clothing, cloth and objects drawn as repeated flat motifs with carved outlines and no shaded folds; small readable block misregistration with thin paper-coloured gaps and slight overlaps; limited Prussian/indigo blue, vermilion, ochre-yellow, muted green, grey-brown and cream palette with black key line. Principal subjects, identities, actions and relationships follow the current brief, not the reference board. Do not add extra people, deities, animals or a new narrative theme. Ordinary supporting scene details and the source-style ornamental motifs may support the requested scene; when the brief sets an exact count or says only, preserve that restricted inventory. Borrow technique, never the reference scene, props, composition or lettering. No text, signature, seal or cartouche unless the brief explicitly asks for exact lettering.
hard_constraints: Black key lines are confident and even-weight, solid opaque black, carved with blunt rounded ends, a few tiny angular knife nicks, rough ink edges and faint wood-grain streaks inside large black areas; avoid sketchy, scratchy, hatched or varying-pressure pen strokes.

Colour areas are flat opaque block-printed fields with crisp edges; tone variation appears only as soft bokashi at sky, water or cloth-hem edges, never on faces, skin, hands, food, tableware or furniture.

Faces and hands present in the brief are flat simplified carved-line shapes with the age and expression of the brief; avoid large round eyes, cute moe or manga proportions, anime sparkle, storybook faces, 3D rounded faces, glossy highlights, soft blush, gradient or airbrush.
When the brief calls for eye contact, both faces turn toward each other with both eyes visible and gaze aimed at the other; a smile must not be drawn as closed arc eyes that hide eye contact.
Flat colour and decorative flat motifs replace volume shading: no photographic light, 3D shading, soft shadow, grey shadow modelling, airbrush gradients or neon/metallic colours.

Space is flattened as in ukiyo-e, with a bold asymmetrical layout, compressed depth, cropped bands and patterned flat motifs; ordinary decorative background and ornamental flower/leaf elements are allowed only when supported by the brief or original definition, and must not introduce new figures, deities, identities or themes.

Visible washi paper shows long wispy plant fibres and faint cloudy ink-absorption mottling; when the brief gives no setting, the ground behind the subject is plain unprinted washi with no added room, scenery or decorative background.
Slight block misregistration is visible: thin paper-coloured gaps between colour plates and the black line along some edges, and small overlaps on others, without blurring faces or hands.
The picture carries no signature, seal, cartouche or lettering except text the brief explicitly requests, spelled exactly as given; never copy reference-board text or fake characters.

Keep the source palette roles of Prussian/indigo blue, vermilion, ochre-yellow, muted green, cream washi ground and black key line; no neon, no metallic. A cheerful festive palette does not require every object to contain every colour.

anchor.isolation: Transfer only the woodblock carved ink outlines, limited flat color plates, washi fibers and compressed perspective technique from this reference board. Do not reproduce its writing, labels, grid, border, sample figures, scenery or layout. Do not copy any content of the reference board: its people, animals (such as its sleeping cat), cups and vessels, books, window, reading room, furniture, decorative layout, poses or arrangement. Draw people, animals, cups, books, windows, rooms or furniture only when the current brief itself asks for them, and then compose them fresh from the brief's own wording, never from the board's scene. When the brief gives no setting, use the washi paper fibre ground of the technique instead of adding a room or scenery from the board. Principal subjects, identities, actions and relationships follow the current brief, not the reference board. Do not add extra people, deities, animals or a new narrative theme. Ordinary supporting scene details and the source-style ornamental motifs may support the requested scene; when the brief sets an exact count or says only, preserve that restricted inventory. Borrow technique, never the reference scene, props, composition or lettering.; reproduce no writing from the board, and add text only where the brief explicitly requests it, spelled exactly as given. The reference is an abstract material proof, not a background design for the new picture. Do not copy any of its individual black strokes, colour-plate silhouettes, fan-like arrangement, intersections, colour positions or crop. Recut all linework and reprint all ink marks for the current brief from scratch; transfer the craft, not the same shapes. When the brief specifies no setting, show only an unprinted plain washi-paper ground behind the subject: no coloured background plates, no black background rays, no abstract decorative background pattern. When the brief requests a setting or ornamental content, construct it only from those requested elements, with fresh shapes and placement; never use the proof layout as a scene or backdrop.
